web.description:
# World population In [world demographics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_the_world), the **world population** is the total number of humans currently alive. It was estimated by the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations) to have [exceeded 8 billion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day_of_Eight_Billion) (8,000,000,000) on November 15, 2022. As of 2026, the world population is approximately 8.3 billion. [[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_population#cite_note-6) The [UN Department of Economics and Social Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Department_of_Economics_and_Social_Affairs) (UNDESA) has projected the world population to reach between 9 and 10 billion people by 2050, providing an 80% [confidence interval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confidence_interval) of 10–12 billion by the end of the 21st century,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_population#cite_note-:4-1) with a growth rate by then of zero. ## Largest populations by country ### Ten most populous countries | # | Most populous countries | 2000 | 2015 | 2030[[A]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_population#cite_note-note-2030-105) | Y axisX axis0300600900120015001800200020152030ChinaIndiaUnited StatesIndonesiaPakistanBrazilNigeriaBangladeshRussiaMexicoTen most populous countries [raw data](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Data:Ten%20most%20populous%20countries.tab) | |-|-|-|-|-|-| | | **World total** | 6,127 | 7,349 | 8,501 | ## Fluctuation ### Past population | Year | World | Africa | Asia | Europe | Latin America

[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_population#cite_note-Kapitza2-14) Kapitsa (1996) cites estimates ranging between 80 and 150billion. [[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_population#cite_note-164) The [PRB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_Reference_Bureau) puts the figure at 117billion as of 2020, estimating that the current world population is 6.7% of all the humans who have lived since 190,000 BCE. [[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_population#cite_note-165) Haub (1995) prepared another figure, updated in 2002 and 2011; the 2011 figure was approximately 107billion.

# Population
## Our growing population
### [Day of Eight Billion](https://www.un.org/en/dayof8billion)
On 15 November 2022, the world’s population [reached 8 billion people](https://www.unfpa.org/sites/default/files/swop23/SWOP2023-ENGLISH-230329-web.pdf), a milestone in human development.
